newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer sees 1997 profits in line with 1996.
newsitem.headline: Bayer sees 1997 profits in line with 1996.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG said on Wednesday it expected profits in 1997 to be at least in line with 1996's 2.7 billion marks ($1.2 trillion) and said it expected 1997 group sales of over 50 billion marks.

The forecast was more downbeat than last month, when the group said it had a realistic chance of topping 1996 profits this year, and profits and sales for this year were at the lower end of analysts' expectations.
Bayer's first quarter 1997 pre-tax profits rose five percent to 1.218 billion marks on turnover of 13.172 billion marks, up from 12.176 billion, Bayer said.
Sales in 1996 totalled 48.6 billion marks, the group said at its annual shareholder meeting.
Market players were disappointed at Bayer's performance and the firm's shares fell after the figures were announced. Initially the stock was down 1.14 percent or 80 pfennigs at 69.40 marks.

In bourse trade the share stood at 96 marks, up two pfennigs on Tuesday's close, but significantly underperformed the overall DAX index of 30 German blue-chips which was up 1.83 percent, 61.84 points, at 3,445 points.
"The figures were a big disappointment," said one trader, who said that sales should have risen further, given the group's improved economic conditions.
Bayer said first-quarter parent company pre-tax profit dipped to 650 million marks from 680 million, on sales up at 4.852 billion marks from 4.685 billion.
